Dombrad Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Dombrád, Hungary

Not demolished. Dombrád's Jewish community, first recorded with 9 residents in an 1770 tax list, grew mainly through Galician migration, peaking at 329 by 1910 before declining to 193 by 1941. Jews here worked chiefly in trade (potatoes, tobacco) and crafts, and owned the local distillery, mill, sawmill, and herb-processing plant; an elementary school opened in the 1890s. Rabbi Chaim Friedmann led the community from 1911, succeeded by Leichtag Efraim in 1920, who remained until the 1944 deportation - his remains were later exhumed and reburied in Israel by descendants. Twelve local Jews died in WWI. Of 200 Jews deported to Auschwitz from Kisvárda in May 1944, only 67 survived; no Jews have lived in Dombrád since the 1960s, and a community center now occupies the former synagogue site. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with its newest tombstone dated 1942.
